Rashi on Makkot 2a:1:1.english: How are witnesses rendered conspiring [witnesses], etc. - In the Gemara, it explains what [the Tanna] is saying.

Rashi on Makkot 2a:1:2.english: [With regard to] so-and-so - [Who is] a priest.

Rashi on Makkot 2a:1:3.hebrew: שהוא בן גרושה - בפנינו נתגרשה אמו קודם שנולד, והרי הוא חלל ופסול (יבמות יב):
Rashi on Makkot 2a:1:3.english: That he is the son of a divorced woman - In our presence his mother was divorced before he was born, and behold, he is a chalal and disqualified [from the priesthood] (Yevamot 12).

Rashi on Makkot 2a:1:4.hebrew: אין אומרים - אם הוזמו והן כהנים, יעשה זה בן גרשה וחלוצה לקיים בו כאשר זמם, אלא סופג את הארבעים. ובגמרא מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Makkot 2a:1:4.english: One does not say - [that] if they were rendered conspiring witnesses and they are priests, this [witness] shall be made the son of a divorced woman or a ḥalutza to fulfill with regard to him [the verse]: "as he conspired" — rather, he receives the forty [lashes]. And in the Gemara, it explains the reason.

Rashi on Makkot 2a:2:1.english: That he is liable to exile - For he killed a person unwittingly.

Rashi on Makkot 2a:3:1.hebrew: ה"ג: האי "כיצד אין העדים נעשין זוממין" מיבעי ליה! ועוד, דקתני לקמן (מכות דף ה.): "אבל אמרו להם" כו':
Rashi on Makkot 2a:3:1.english: This is the correct reading: This [phrase in the Mishnah] should have read: "How do witnesses not become conspiring [witnesses]?" And furthermore, since it teaches later (Makkot 5a): "But if they said to them," etc.

Rashi on Makkot 2a:3:2.hebrew: כיצד אין העדים נעשין זוממין מיבעי ליה - דהא לא מקיימת בהו "כאשר זמם":
Rashi on Makkot 2a:3:2.english: [The Tanna] should have [taught]: How are the witnesses not rendered conspiring [witnesses] - For [the law of doing to them] "as he conspired" (Deuteronomy 19:19) is not fulfilled with regard to them.

Rashi on Makkot 2a:3:3.hebrew: ועוד - מאי קא בעי תנא "כיצד נעשין זוממין"? הא קתני לה לקמן כיצד דין זוממין, דקתני במתני': "אבל אמרו להם המזימים: היאך אתם מעידים עדות זה? והלא הייתם עמנו אותו היום במקום פלוני" כו':
Rashi on Makkot 2a:3:3.english: And furthermore - Why does the Tanna ask, "How do [witnesses] become conspiring [witnesses]"? Behold, he teaches it later how the law of conspiring [witnesses] [operates], for he teaches in the Mishnah: "But [if] those rendering them conspiring said to them: 'How can you testify [to] this testimony? Were you not with us on that day in such-and-such a place?'" etc.

Rashi on Makkot 2a:4:1.hebrew: התם קאי - מסנהדרין סליק, דתנן בשילהי אלו הן הנחנקין — דהוא סיומא דסנהדרין — דיש זוממין שנשתנו במקצת מדין הזמה, כדקתני: כל הזוממין מקדימים לאותה מיתה. כלומר, אין להם לצפות מיתה אחרת, אלא משכימין לאותה מיתה שנגמר בה דינו של נדון:
Rashi on Makkot 2a:4:1.english: He is standing there - He has just concluded [Tractate] Sanhedrin, for we learned in a Mishnah at the end of [the chapter entitled] "These Are the Ones Who Are Strangled" — which is the conclusion of Sanhedrin — that there are conspiring witnesses who differ somewhat from the [standard] law of conspiracy, as it teaches: "All conspiring witnesses go early to that [same] death." That is to say, they do not await a different death; rather, they go early to that [same] death to which the accused was sentenced.

Rashi on Makkot 2a:4:2.hebrew: חוץ מזוממי בת כהן - נשואה, שאע"פ שנגמר דינה לשריפה על פיהם, הם בחנק, כדילפינן התם (דף צ.): "היא בשריפה" — ואין בועלה בשריפה, אלא בחנק כשאר אשת איש; והזוממין משכימין למיתה שחייבו את הבועל, דכתיב: "כאשר זמם לעשות לאחיו" — ולא לאחותו (שם). וקאמר הכא: עוד יש זוממין אחרים שאין מקיימין בהן דין הזמה כלל, אלא מלקות; ועלה מפרש: "כיצד" אותן "העדים" שאין מקיימין בהן דין הזמה "נעשין זוממין? מעידים אנו כו'":
Rashi on Makkot 2a:4:2.english: Except for conspiring [witnesses] of the daughter of a priest - [who is] married; for even though her sentence was finalized for burning on the basis of their testimony, they are [executed] by strangulation, as we derive there (Sanhedrin 90a): "She [shall be burnt] in fire" — and her paramour is not [executed] by burning, but rather by strangulation like [the paramour of] any other married woman; and the conspiring witnesses are led early to the mode of execution to which they sought to subject the paramour, as it is written: "as he conspired to do to his brother" — and not "to his sister" (ibid.). And [the tanna] states here: Furthermore, there are other conspiring witnesses upon whom we do not fulfill the law of conspiracy [retaliation] at all, but rather lashes; and concerning this he explains: "How" are those "witnesses" upon whom we do not fulfill the law of conspiracy "rendered conspiring witnesses? [They say:] 'We testify, etc.'"

Rashi on Makkot 2a:6:1.hebrew: ולא לזרעו - ואם תעשהו חלל והוא כהן, פסלת את זרעו לעולם:
Rashi on Makkot 2a:6:1.english: But not to his offspring - And if you make him a chalal when he is a priest, you have disqualified his offspring forever.

Rashi on Makkot 2a:6:2.english: We require “as he conspired” - And he conspired to disqualify the one being judged and his offspring.

Rashi on Makkot 2a:7:1.hebrew: המחלל אינו מתחלל - כהן הנושא את הגרושה, שמחלל את זרעו, אין הוא עצמו מתחלל מן הכהונה:
Rashi on Makkot 2a:7:1.english: One who disqualifies is not [himself] disqualified - A priest who marries a divorcée, who disqualifies his offspring, is not himself disqualified from the priesthood.

Rashi on Makkot 2a:7:2.hebrew: הבא לחלל ולא חילל - עד זומם שרצה לחלל ולא חיללו, אינו דין כו':
Rashi on Makkot 2a:7:2.english: One who came to disqualify and did not disqualify - A conspiring witness who wanted to disqualify [another from the priesthood] and did not disqualify him — is it not logical, etc.?

Rashi on Makkot 2a:7:3.hebrew: אם כן - אם באת לדרוש ק"ו זה בעדים זוממים, בטלת תורת הזמתם:
Rashi on Makkot 2a:7:3.english: If so - If you come to expound this a fortiori inference regarding conspiring witnesses, you have abolished the law of their refutation.

Tosafot on Makkot 2a:1:1.hebrew: מעידין אנו באיש פלוני שהוא בן גרושה או בן חלוצה אין אומרים כו' - תימה, כיון דאם הוזמו אינן נעשין בן גרושה וחלוצה, א"כ גם בשלא יוזמו איך יעשה על פיהם בן גרושה? דהכי הוא האמת! ואמאי? הא הויא לה עדות שאי אתה יכול להזימה, ואין זה עדות! וי"ל, כיון דלוקין הוי "כאשר זמם", והוי שפיר אתה יכול להזימה. וקשה, דא"כ מאי קאמר פרק היו בודקין (סנהדרין דף מא.) גבי עדי נערה המאורסה: דאיהי לא מיקטלא, דכיון דאינהו לא מיקטלי משום שיכולין לומר "לאסרה על בעלה באנו", והויא לה עדות שאי אתה יכול להזימה? ומאי קאמר, והא מ"מ לוקין! וי"ל, דהתם כיון שבאין לחייבה מיתה וזממו להרוג את הנפש, לא מיקיים "כאשר זמם" במלקות, דהא בהדיא כתיב "נפש בנפש" גבי הזמה דעדות נפשות, ולא חשיב יכול להזימה במלקות. אבל הכא, שלא כוון אלא לשווייה בן גרושה ובן חלוצה, דליכא כי אם לאו בעלמא — כיון שלקו, חשיב שפיר עדות שאתה יכול להזימה. ועי"ל, דגבי עדות דבן גרושה וחלוצה לא חיישינן כלל באתה יכול להזימה; דמהיכא נפקא לן דבעינן עדות שאתה יכול להזימה? מ"כאשר זמם"! והא מוכח בגמרא ד"כאשר זמם" לא נכתב לגבי עדות דבן גרושה, ולא קאי כלל עליה בשום צד שבעולם. אבל התם גבי נערה המאורסה, ודאי "כאשר זמם" קאי נמי עליהן, דאם התרו בה מיקטלי אינהו בשהוזמו, ואילו איהי בלא הוזמו; והתם מיירי בלא התרו, וכיון ד"כאשר זמם" קאי עלייהו, לכך בעינן אתה יכול להזימה. ויש לדקדק: אמאי לא נקט "מעידין אנו באיש פלוני שהוא ממזר כו'"? דזה הוה שייך בין בישראל בין בכהנים, ובן גרושה לא פסיל אלא בכהנים! ויש ליישב, דנקטיה משום דקאי אזוממי בת כהן, כדאיתא בגמרא, ולכך נקט מידי דשייך בכהונה:
Tosafot on Makkot 2a:1:1.english: "We testify with regard to so-and-so that he is the son of a divorced woman or the son of a chalutzah," one does not say, etc. - This is puzzling: since if they are rendered conspiring witnesses [zomemin], they are not made the son of a divorced woman or a chalutzah, if so, even when they are not rendered zomemin, how can he be made the son of a divorced woman based on their testimony — for such is in fact the law! Why should this be so? Behold, it is a testimony that you cannot subject to hazamah [retributive punishment for conspiracy], and that is not valid testimony! And one can answer that since they receive lashes, this constitutes "as he schemed" (Deuteronomy 19:19), and it is properly considered [a testimony that] you can subject to hazamah. Yet this is difficult: for if so, what is it that [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Hayu Bodkin (Sanhedrin 41a) regarding witnesses against a betrothed young woman — that she is not executed because they themselves cannot be executed, as they can say, "We came only to render her forbidden to her husband," and it is therefore a testimony that you cannot subject to hazamah? What is it saying? Behold, they receive lashes in any case! And one can answer that there, since they come to make her liable to the death penalty and schemed to take a life, "as he schemed" is not fulfilled through lashes — for "life for life" (Deuteronomy 19:21) is explicitly written regarding the hazamah of capital testimony — and it is not considered [a testimony that] you can subject to hazamah by virtue of lashes. Here, however, where one intended only to render him the son of a divorced woman or the son of a chalutzah, which involves nothing more than a mere negative prohibition, once they receive lashes it is properly considered a testimony that you can subject to hazamah. And one can further answer that regarding testimony about the son of a divorced woman or a chalutzah, we are not concerned at all with whether you can subject it to hazamah. For from where do we derive that we require testimony that you can subject to hazamah? From "as he schemed"! And it is proven in the Gemara that "as he schemed" was not written regarding testimony about the son of a divorced woman, and does not apply to it at all in any way whatsoever. There, however, regarding a betrothed young woman, "as he schemed" certainly applies to them as well: for had they forewarned her, they would be executed when rendered zomemin, whereas she [would be executed] when they were not rendered zomemin; and there it deals with a case where they did not forewarn [her], and since "as he schemed" applies to them [in principle], we therefore require that you be able to subject [their testimony] to hazamah. And one may further inquire: why did [the Tanna] not state, "We testify with regard to so-and-so that he is a mamzer, etc."? For that would apply both to Israelites and to priests, whereas being the son of a divorced woman disqualifies only priests! And one can resolve that he stated this case because [the Mishnah] is referring back to the conspiring witnesses against the daughter of a priest, as stated in the Gemara, and therefore he chose something that pertains to the priesthood.

Tosafot on Makkot 2a:2:1.hebrew: מעידין אנו באיש פלוני שחייב גלות - וא"ת: היאך הם יכולים לחייבו גלות בעדותן, והא יכול לומר "מזיד הייתי", כדאמר גבי "אכלת חלב" בפ"ק דבבא מציעא (דף ג:)? וי"ל דמיירי כשראו בו רגלים לדבר שנשמט הברזל מקתו, ואיכא למימר דלא נתכוין. אבל קשה מהא דתנן פרק אלו הן הגולין (לקמן מכות דף ט.) דשונא אינו גולה — לאו כי האי גוונא דומיא דאוהב גולה? ואמאי אינו גולה כיון דראו דהוי רגלים לדבר? וי"ל דשאני שונא, דיש לנו לומר טפי דבשנאה הכהו. ועוד י"ל דמיירי שפיר דליכא רגלים לדבר, והשתא ניחא משונא; ומ"מ אוהב גולה, כגון דשתיק כשאמרו לו העדים. בודאי אי הוה אמר "לא הרגתיו", יכול לתרץ ולומר "לא הרגתיו שוגג אלא מזיד", כמו ב"לא אכלתי חלב"; אבל כיון דשתק, כהודאה דמיא:
Tosafot on Makkot 2a:2:1.english: "We testify with regard to so-and-so that he is liable to exile" - And if you ask: How can they render him liable to exile through their testimony, when he can say, "I was intentional," just as the Gemara says concerning witnesses who tell a person, "You ate forbidden fat," in the first chapter of Bava Metzia (3b) that a person is not obligated to bring a sin-offering if he claims he ate it intentionally? One can answer that our Mishnah is dealing with a case where the witnesses saw circumstantial evidence indicating that the iron ax head slipped from its handle, so that there are grounds to say that he did not intend to kill him. However, there is a difficulty from that which we learned in a Mishnah in the chapter Eilu Hein HaGolin (below, Makkot 9a), that an enemy does not go into exile. Is that not in such a case, parallel to a friend who goes into exile? And why does he not go into exile, since they saw that there is circumstantial evidence that it was unintentional? One can answer that an enemy is different, for we have more reason to say that he struck him out of hatred. Furthermore, one can answer that our Mishnah is indeed dealing with a case where there is no circumstantial evidence, and now the difficulty from an enemy is resolved; and nevertheless, a friend goes into exile in a case where he remained silent when the witnesses spoke their testimony against him. Certainly, had he said, "I did not kill him," he could have reinterpreted his words and said, "I did not kill him unwittingly, but rather intentionally," just as with "I did not eat forbidden fat"; however, since he remained silent, it is tantamount to an admission.

Tosafot on Makkot 2a:3:1.hebrew: ועוד מדקתני לקמן - פיר' הקונטרס: דמאי בעי "כיצד וכו'"? הא קתני לקמן וכו'! ועוד יש לפרש: "ועוד" — כלומר, ואם תמצא לומר דלשון הזמה הוא, זה אינו, דעל כרחך דין הזמה קאמר כדקתני, ולאלומי קושייתא קמייתא:
Tosafot on Makkot 2a:3:1.english: And furthermore, from [the fact] that it teaches later - The Kuntres (Rashi) explained: Why does [the tanna] ask, "How [are witnesses rendered conspiring witnesses], etc."? Behold, it teaches later, etc. [how they are rendered conspiring witnesses]! And furthermore, one can explain: "And furthermore" — that is to say, even if you should say that [the opening question of the Mishnah] refers to the terminology [or verbal formula] of rendering witnesses conspiring (hazamah), this is not so; for perforce it is speaking of the law of rendering witnesses conspiring, as it teaches [later], and [this comes] to strengthen the first difficulty.

Tosafot on Makkot 2a:4:1.hebrew: כל הזוממין מקדימין לאותה מיתה - פי' הקונטרס: שאין להם נס והמלטה. וקשה, דמאי קמ"ל? פשיטא! ובכתובות פירש שרוצה לומר "מקדימין" — שלא יענו הדין. וגם זה קשה, דמאי קמ"ל? פשיטא! לכך פירש ר"י: "מקדימין", הכי פירושו: ודאי אתה צריך להמיתן במיתה שהמיתו, אבל ודאי אם אינו יכול, אפ"ה נמיתם בכל מיתה שנוכל, כדתניא: "הכה תכה" (ב"מ דף לא:). וקשה, דאמרינן פרק נגמר הדין (סנהדרין דף מה:) דרוצח וגואל הדם הוו ב' כתובין הבאין כאחד! וכן קשה, דבתוספתא (פי"ב דסנהדרין) תניא: "אבל הזוממין, שאין אתה יכול להמיתן במיתה הכתובה בהן, אתה ממיתם בכל מיתה", ודריש ליה מן קרא ד"ובערת הרע מקרבך", ואמאי הוי רוצח וגואל הדם ב' כתובין הבאים כאחד? ותירץ ה"ר יוסף, דרוצח וגואל הדם הוו ב' כתובים הבאין כאחד לענין שלא נלמוד שאר מומתין מהם להמיתם אף במיתה שאינה מד' מיתות ב"ד; אבל מד' מיתות ב"ד, פשיטא נמיתם ככל חייבי מיתות:
Tosafot on Makkot 2a:4:1.english: All conspiring witnesses are led first [makdimin] to that execution - The Commentary [Rashi] explained: that they have no escape or deliverance [from that execution]. And this is difficult, for what does this teach us? It is obvious! And in Ketubot [33b] he explained that "makdimin" means that they should not delay the judgment. And this too is difficult, for what does this teach us? It is obvious! Therefore, the Ri explained: "makdimin" — this is its meaning: Initially [as the primary preference], you must certainly execute them with the execution with which they sought to execute [the accused]; however, if one certainly cannot [do so], even so we execute them with whatever execution we can, as it is taught in a baraita: "You shall surely strike [hakkeh takkeh]" (Bava Metzia 31b). And this is difficult, for we say in the chapter [entitled] Nigmar HaDin (Sanhedrin 45b) that a murderer and the redeemer of blood constitute two verses that come as one [teaching the same law, and therefore cannot teach that other condemned offenders may be executed by any available means]! And it is similarly difficult, for in the Tosefta (Sanhedrin, Chapter 12) it is taught: "However, regarding conspiring witnesses whom you cannot execute with the execution written concerning them, you execute them with any execution," and it derives this from the verse, "and you shall eradicate the evil from your midst" [Deuteronomy 19:19] — and [if so,] why do a murderer and the redeemer of blood constitute two verses that come as one? And Rabbi Yosef answered that a murderer and the redeemer of blood constitute two verses that come as one with respect to not deriving from them that other condemned offenders may be executed even with a manner of death that is not one of the four court-imposed executions; however, from among the four court-imposed executions, it is obvious that we execute them, just like all others liable to court-imposed executions.

Tosafot on Makkot 2a:4:2.hebrew: זוממי בת כהן ובועלה שאין מקדימין לאותה מיתה אלא למיתה אחרת - בועלה — דדרשינן: "היא" ולא בועלה, וזוממי בת כהן — דכתיב "לאחיו", דדרשינן: "לאחיו" ולא לאחותו. וא"ת: למה לי דרשא ד"לאחיו" ולא לאחותו? תיפוק ליה מ"היא", דנפקא לן דדרשינן (סנהדרין נא.): "את אביה היא מחללת" — "היא" ולא בועלה, "היא" ולא זוממיה! וי"ל: הואיל וזוממיה באו לחייבה שריפה, לא יבא לאוקומי מיעוטא ד"היא" אלא בבועלה, ולא ממעטינן זוממין (אלא מן "אחיו"); אבל כיון דכתיב "אחיו", דרשינן נמי מ"היא" למעוטי זוממיה. אבל קשה: כיון דכתיב "אחיו", אמאי איצטריך למעוטי זוממין מ"היא"? וי"ל: דאי מ"אחיו", הוה אמינא דה"מ כשהבועל היה נדון קרינן ביה "לאחיו", אבל אם לא היה נדון על פי עדותן — כגון שהיה קטן בן ט' שנים ויום אחד, או שלא הכירו הבועל — לא קרינן ביה "לאחיו"; קמ"ל "היא" ולא זוממין, למעוטי זוממין בכל ענין. ומתחלה היה ר"י מסופק בהאי מילתא, ושוב פשטה מפרק נגמר הדין (סנהדרין דף מו.), דקאמר: מיתה אחת מעין שתי מיתות — כגון בת כהן ובועלה, או בת כהן וזוממי זוממין. והשתא, למה ליה זוממי זוממין? תיפוק ליה דאיכא שתי מיתות בלא זוממי זוממין, משום הבועל שהוא בחנק! אלא שמע מינה דאיירי כגון דליכא דין מיתה בבועלה, כגון שהוא קטן כדפירשתי, ואפ"ה קאמרי זוממי זוממין בחנק; אלמא דהוה זוממין בחנק אע"פ דליכא דין מיתה בבועל: ועוד מדקתני לקמן - פיר' הקונטרס: דמאי בעי "כיצד וכו'"? הא קתני לקמן וכו'! ועוד יש לפרש: "ועוד", כלומר: ואם תמצא לומר דלשון הזמה הוא, זה אינו, דעל כרחך דין הזמה קאמר כדקתני, ולאלומי קושייתא קמייתא:
Tosafot on Makkot 2a:4:2.english: The conspiring witnesses against the daughter of a priest and her paramour, who are not led to the same mode of execution, but rather to a different mode of execution - Her paramour [is executed by strangulation rather than burning] because we expound: "She [shall be burned with fire]" (Leviticus 21:9) — and not her paramour; and the conspiring witnesses against the daughter of a priest [are executed by strangulation, the paramour's mode of execution, rather than burning] because it is written: "[to do] to his brother" (Deuteronomy 19:19), which we expound: "to his brother" — and not to his sister. And if you ask: Why do I need the exposition of "to his brother" — and not to his sister? Let it be derived from "she," from which we derive when we expound (Sanhedrin 51a): "She profanes her father" — "she," and not her paramour; "she," and not her conspiring witnesses! And one can answer: Since her conspiring witnesses came to make her liable to burning, one would not come to apply the exclusion of "she" except to her paramour, and we would not exclude conspiring witnesses (except from "his brother"); however, once "his brother" is written, we also expound from "she" to exclude her conspiring witnesses. However, it is difficult: Since "his brother" is written, why was it necessary to exclude conspiring witnesses from "she"? And one can answer: Had it been derived [only] from "his brother," I would have said that this applies only when the paramour was subject to judgment — [in which case] we apply to him "to his brother"; however, if he was not subject to judgment on the basis of their testimony — such as where he was a minor nine years and one day old, or where they did not recognize the paramour — we do not apply to him "to his brother." Therefore, [the exposition] "'she' — and not conspiring witnesses" informs us to exclude conspiring witnesses [from burning, subjecting them to strangulation] in every case. Initially, Rabbeinu Yitzchak was in doubt about this matter, and subsequently he resolved it from the chapter [entitled] Nigmar HaDin (Sanhedrin 46a), where it says: "One mode of execution that resembles two modes of execution — such as the daughter of a priest and her paramour, or the daughter of a priest and the conspiring witnesses of her conspiring witnesses." Now, why does it need [to mention] the conspiring witnesses of her conspiring witnesses? Let it emerge that there are two modes of execution without the conspiring witnesses of her conspiring witnesses, on account of the paramour, who is [executed] by strangulation! Rather, learn from this that it is dealing with a case where there is no law of execution for her paramour, such as where he is a minor, as I explained, and even so they say that the conspiring witnesses of her conspiring witnesses are [executed] by strangulation; thus we see that the conspiring witnesses are [executed] by strangulation even though there is no law of execution for the paramour. And furthermore, from that which [the Tanna] teaches later - The Kuntres explained: Why does [the Tanna] ask "How [are witnesses rendered conspiring witnesses], etc."? Behold, he teaches later [how they are rendered conspiring witnesses], etc.! And furthermore, one can explain: "And furthermore" — that is to say, if you should say that ["how are witnesses rendered conspiring witnesses" in our Mishnah] refers merely to the terminology of being rendered conspiring witnesses, this is not so; for perforce it refers to the law [and reciprocal punishment] of conspiring testimony, as it teaches [later: "these are conspiring witnesses," implying that those in our Mishnah are not subject to the law of conspiring witnesses], and [this is adduced] to strengthen the first difficulty.

Tosafot on Makkot 2a:6:1.hebrew: בעינן כאשר זמם וליכא - קשיא: היכא שמעידין שהוא מצרי שני, דאינן באין לפסול זרעו כי אם לפסלו — א"כ נפסול! וי"ל דמ"מ אשתו נפסלת, דפסלה בביאתו, וכתיב: "ועשיתם לו כאשר זמם" — "לו", ולא לאשתו:
Tosafot on Makkot 2a:6:1.english: We require "as he conspired," and that is not [the case] - This is difficult: Where they testify that he is a second-generation Egyptian, in which case they do not come to disqualify his offspring [who would be third-generation Egyptians and thus permitted], but only to disqualify him — if so, let him [the witness] be disqualified! And one can say that nevertheless, his [the witness's] wife would be disqualified, as he disqualifies her through his cohabitation, and it is written: "And you shall do to him as he conspired" — "to him," and not to his wife.
